title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: permission sync in incremental crawls
notes: claim 58: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing and connector-specific permission-sync descriptions are supported. It should avoid implying a guaranteed permission-update interval, acknowledge conflicting Confluence On-premises documentation, and remove the unsupported assertion that users see no new surface.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends periodic full crawls even when incremental crawls are used.
claims.quote: Even when you use incremental refreshes, run full refreshes periodically to ensure data consistency between the source system and the search index.

claims.claim: The Confluence Cloud deployment page says incremental crawls do not pick up ACL changes.
claims.quote: Incremental crawls don't pick up ACL changes or deleted items.

claims.claim: Copilot grounds answers on indexed connector content.
claims.quote: The conversational Copilot Chat experience in Microsoft Copilot, Teams, Outlook, and other Microsoft 365 apps use connector content to respond to user queries.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview to sources for the grounding and indexed-item ACL statements in Why it matters.

claims.claim: Each indexed connector item carries access rules from the source system.
claims.quote: Each item includes content, metadata (like title and URL), and an access control list (ACL) that enforces permissions.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview for this sentence; its permission-based filtering passage also says Search and Copilot only show items to users who have access in the source system.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where incremental crawls skip permission updates, revoked source access can remain reflected incorrectly in the index until the next full crawl.
claims.quote: Changes to permissions in Vault might not instantly reflect in the index; if a permission is revoked, there can be a delay until the next full crawl.

claims.claim: For connectors with incremental permission handling, the stale-permission window shrinks to the incremental interval.
claims.quote: checks for identity changes, such as new or removed users, role assignments, group memberships, and user criteria attributes, and updates permissions between full crawls.
claims.fix: Replace 'Where a connector now does that in incremental crawls, the window shrinks from the full-crawl interval (generally a day, per the roadmap item) to the incremental interval.' with 'Where a connector supports the relevant permission change in incremental crawls, that change can be processed between full crawls.' The cited deployment overview says system load can delay crawl start times by up to an hour; the configured interval is not a guaranteed completion time.

claims.claim: Synced connectors index external content on a recurring schedule.
claims.quote: **Synced connectors** index content from an external data source into the Microsoft 365 substrate on a recurring schedule.

claims.claim: Federated connectors query data at runtime without indexing, so indexed-content crawl schedules do not apply.

claims.claim: Configuring and managing connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center requires the AI administrator role.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > data source > Custom setup > Sync reaches full and incremental crawl scheduling.
claims.quote: On the **Connectors** tab, in the left pane, choose **Gallery**, and select the data source you want to connect ... select **Custom setup** ... On the **Sync** tab, you can configure how often data syncs between the source and the connector index.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Connectors tab > Gallery > data source > Custom setup > Sync'. The omitted Connectors tab is the tab listing the connector gallery; the printed steps are otherwise in the documented order.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for setting the prebuilt connection's full and incremental crawl schedule is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph Copilot connector crawl schedule sync configuration API beta externalConnection update'; opened externalConnection update in v1.0 and beta, deployment-overview and manage-connector. No schedule-setting operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > data source > Custom setup > Users > Access Permissions reaches the connection-creation visibility setting.
claims.quote: On the **Connectors** tab ... choose **Gallery**, and select the data source ... select **Custom setup** ... On the **Users** tab, under **Access Permissions**, choose whether indexed data is visible to: Only users with access to the content; Everyone in the organization
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Copilot > Connectors > Connectors tab > Gallery > data source > Custom setup > Users > Access Permissions'. This is the creation path documented by the cited page, not an edit-in-place path for a published connection.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for the connection-level Everyone versus source-access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot connectors access permissions Everyone Only people admin center API setting externalConnection acl'; opened manage-access-permissions and externalConnection update v1.0/beta. External-item ACL APIs do not set this connection-level visibility choice.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Source permission sync governs visibility when the connection respects source access, whereas Everyone exposes indexed data to all organization users.
claims.quote: If you choose **Everyone**, indexed data appears in the search results for all users. If you choose **Only people with access to this data source**, search results respect the same permission setup as the data source.

claims.claim: The Map Identities section on the Users tab configures how source users are matched to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: By default, the system maps users by matching their email to `UserPrincipalName` or `Mail` in Microsoft Entra ID. In the **Map Identities** section, you can provide a custom mapping formula.

claims.claim: Existing synced connections and their configured access permissions can be reviewed under Copilot > Connectors.
claims.quote: go to **Copilot** > **Connectors** > **Your Connections**. ... Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. ... Under **Permissions**, you can view the permissions set for the connector.
claims.fix: Replace the first Before rollout bullet with 'List each synced connection under Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections, select the connection, and review Permissions to see whether it respects source access or is visible to everyone.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/manage-access-permissions.
